LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 7.1.2 PRONUNCIATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.1: Listening and Speaking 7.1.2 Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 7.1.2 Pronunciation, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to articulate sounds correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 7.1.2 Pronunciation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: The learner interacts with digital technology with assistive technology as they search online for words

with the sounds /ŋ/ / and the blends / /ŋɡ/.

• Communication: The learner speaks clearly and effectively as they read the sentences in pairs, putting emphasis on

different parts of the sentence to bring out different meanings.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner exercises resilience as they work with others to construct sentences on the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship education: The learner promotes social cohesion as they discuss the effect on meaning when stress is placed on

different parts of the sentence.
